docs.title: UCM Newsletter Builder
docs.text:
The UCM Newsletter Builder is an AI-assisted production pipeline for the University of Idaho's University Communications and Marketing (UCM) office. It streamlines the creation of two campus newsletters:

  • The Daily Register (TDR) -- faculty and staff newsletter, published every weekday
  • My UI -- student newsletter, published weekly on Mondays

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
The system follows a five-stage pipeline:

Submission Intake --> AI Editing --> Human Review --> Newsletter Assembly --> Word Export
  1. Submission Intake -- campus contributors submit announcements through a web form with scheduling preferences, links, and optional images.
  2. AI Editing -- submissions are processed by an LLM (Claude, OpenAI, or MindRouter) guided by UCM style rules stored in the database.
  3. Human Review -- editors review AI suggestions in a side-by-side diff view, accept or revise edits, and finalize copy.
  4. Newsletter Assembly -- finalized items, recurring editorial messages, and imported external content are placed into newsletter sections, reordered, and previewed.
  5. Word Export -- the assembled newsletter is exported to a .docx file matching UCM's existing templates.

docs.title: Tech Stack
docs.text: Layer Technology Frontend React, TypeScript, TailwindCSS v4, Vite Backend FastAPI, Python 3.12+ ORM SQLAlchemy 2.x (async) Database SQLite (development), PostgreSQL (prod) AI Abstracted LLM layer (Claude, OpenAI, MindRouter) Export python-docx Deployment Docker Compose (nginx + uvicorn + PostgreSQL)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Backend
cd backend
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"
alembic upgrade head
python -m app.db.seed
uvicorn app.main:app --port 8001 --reload

# Frontend
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev

Port Note

The backend runs on port 8001 by default. The Vite dev server proxies /api requests to this port.

docs.title: AI Editing Pipeline
docs.text: The AI editing pipeline transforms raw submissions into polished newsletter copy by combining rule-based pre-analysis, LLM-powered rewriting, and deterministic post-processing.

docs.title: Pipeline Stages
docs.text:
Submission text
      |
      v
 Pre-Analysis (rule-based checks)
      |
      v
 Style Rule Loading (from DB)
      |
      v
 LLM Prompt Construction
      |
      v
 LLM Call (Claude, OpenAI, or MindRouter)
      |
      v
 Post-Processing (headline case, diff)
      |
      v
 EditVersion stored (immutable)

docs.title: Pre-Analysis
docs.text:
Before calling the LLM, the pipeline runs deterministic checks to flag common issues:

Check What it detects First-person detection Uses of "I", "we", "our" in body text Exclamation marks Excessive or inappropriate exclamation points Event detail check Missing date, time, or location for events URL validation Broken or malformed links in submission links

Pre-analysis results are passed to the LLM as context so it can address flagged issues in its rewrite.

docs.title: Style Rule Loading
docs.text:
Style rules are stored in the StyleRule table with a Rule_Set column:

  • Shared -- applies to both newsletters
  • TDR -- The Daily Register only
  • MyUI -- My UI only

When editing a submission, the pipeline loads all Shared rules plus the rules for the target newsletter. Rules are grouped by severity (Error, Warning, Suggestion) for prioritized prompt injection.

docs.title: LLM Prompt Construction
docs.text: The prompt sent to the LLM has two parts:

docs.title: System Prompt
docs.text:
Contains the editorial persona and all applicable style rules organized by category:

You are a university communications editor...

## Error-Level Rules (must fix)
- [rule text from DB]
- ...

## Warning-Level Rules (should fix)
- ...

## Suggestion-Level Rules (consider)
- ...

## Pre-Analysis Flags
- First person detected in paragraph 2
- ...

docs.title: User Prompt
docs.text:
Contains the submission text and a before/after example demonstrating the expected transformation style:

Edit the following submission for [newsletter name].

### Example
**Before:** [raw example text]
**After:** [edited example text]

### Submission to Edit
**Title:** [submission title]
**Body:** [submission body]

Few-Shot Learning

The before/after example in the user prompt grounds the LLM's editing style. Future phases may support multiple examples pulled from previously approved edits.

docs.title: Post-Processing
docs.text:
After the LLM returns its suggested edit, deterministic post-processing ensures consistency:

  • Headline case enforcement -- the title is re-cased according to the Headline_Case setting for the target newsletter (Title Case or Sentence Case).
  • Diff generation -- a structured diff between the original text and the AI suggestion is computed and stored as Diff_JSON on the EditVersion record.
  • Whitespace normalization -- trailing spaces, double spaces, and inconsistent line breaks are cleaned up.

docs.title: Editor Review Modes
docs.text:
Once the AI pipeline produces an edit, the editor reviews changes on the AI Suggested tab using one of three modes, selectable via a toggle:

Mode Description Side by Side Two-column layout with the original text on the left and AI-edited text on the right. Useful for reading the full copy in context and judging overall flow. Stacks vertically on small screens. Default view. Inline Diff Word-level diff with red strikethrough (deletions) and green highlights (insertions). Shows exactly what the AI changed, token by token. Live View Editable AI-suggested headline, body, links, and linked-body preview. Editors can save a draft or approve the submission directly, or carry their changes into Final Edit.

All modes display flags and a changes-made summary below the comparison or editor.

docs.title: Two editors, or a slow AI edit
docs.text: Each save names the staff revision the editor's view was loaded with. If another editor saved in the meantime, nothing is saved: the Editor shows the newer version beside the unsaved text, and staff either load the newer version or deliberately save theirs over it. An AI edit that finishes after staff saved or approved the item keeps its suggestion in the history but leaves the status and approval alone; only a submission still awaiting review becomes "AI edited".

docs.title: Interrupted edits and retry
docs.text:
Accepted edits are recorded in ai_edit_tasks before background execution. Poll GET /api/v1/ai-edits/tasks/{task_id} for their durable status and result. A successful task and its edit versions commit together. Completed results remain available after restart; queued/running tasks are marked failed at startup with an interruption message. The Editor keeps polling the same task through brief connection/gateway failures without re-sending the edit request. Staff can run the edit again in the Editor, or retry the same task through POST /api/v1/ai-edits/tasks/{task_id}/retry. Retrying an active or successful task returns its existing state/result without another run. Interrupted external calls are not automatically replayed.

Only one active request per submission/newsletter is admitted. Identical pending requests share a task ID; different instructions receive 409 until it finishes. Source copy, category, target, notes and links are fingerprinted when queued and checked before execution and before saving. A changed source fails the old task; reload and request a fresh edit. Newer staff copy/approval remains authoritative; a suggestion completed after a staff save is retained only as history.

AI_EDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY limits concurrent model calls (default 2), and AI_EDIT_MAX_PENDING limits queued plus running requests (default 50). A full queue returns 503 with Retry-After: 5. The current dispatcher supports the single-process backend used by Compose; do not add workers or replicas without replacing startup recovery and admission with coordinated worker leases.

Task instructions and result JSON may contain unpublished copy or incidental personal data. They follow the parent submission's handling/retention category and are deleted with it. Completed task rows are not cached in process memory. There is no automatic task-history purge or new retention period.

docs.title: Links in Live View and Final Edit
docs.text: Each link pairs a destination with the exact words in the body that carry it. A link stays on the mention it was attached to: editing other text, even typing the same words earlier in the body, does not move it. When the link words appear more than once, a picker under the link lists each mention with its surrounding words so staff can choose which one gets the link. If a link's words are no longer in the body, the link shows a warning and saving is blocked until the words are restored, changed, or the link is cleared, so a link is never dropped silently.

docs.title: Edit Version Storage
docs.text:
Each pipeline run creates an EditVersion record with Version_Type = AI_Suggested. The original submission text is stored in a separate Original version. When an editor finalizes the copy, an Editor_Final version is created. No version is ever modified after creation.

Original  -->  AI_Suggested  -->  Editor_Final

This produces a complete, auditable trail of every change made to a submission.

Saving a final with Approve records that exact version as the submission's approved revision (Approved_Version_Id); saving a draft leaves the submission in review with nothing approved. The Editor reopens, and newsletter assembly publishes, the revision chosen by app/services/editorial_content.py, and each assembled item records the version it was copied from (Source_Version_Id).

docs.title: Provider Abstraction
docs.text:
The LLM provider is selected at startup via the LLM_PROVIDER environment variable:

Value Provider Model (default) Notes claude Anthropic Claude API claude-sonnet-4-20250514 Cloud API, requires API key openai OpenAI API gpt-4o Cloud API, requires API key mindrouter U of I MindRouter (on-prem) moonshotai/kimi-k3 On-prem, OpenAI-compatible API

All providers implement a common LLMProvider interface with two methods:

class LLMProvider(ABC):
    async def complete(
        self,
        system_prompt: str,
        user_prompt: str,
        temperature: float = 0.3,
        max_tokens: int = 2000,
    ) -> LLMResponse: ...

    async def complete_json(
        self,
        system_prompt: str,
        user_prompt: str,
        temperature: float = 0.2,
        max_tokens: int = 2000,
    ) -> dict: ...

Switching providers requires only changing the environment variable and restarting the backend. No code changes are needed.

docs.title: MindRouter Details
docs.text:
MindRouter is the University of Idaho's institutional AI services platform, hosted at mindrouter.uidaho.edu. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint, which the MindRouterProvider calls using httpx.

Key implementation details:

  • <think> block stripping -- Qwen3 models emit reasoning tokens wrapped in <think>...</think> tags before their actual response. The provider strips these automatically.
  • Markdown fence stripping -- JSON responses sometimes arrive wrapped in ```json ... ``` fences, which are removed before parsing.
  • Timeout -- 120-second timeout for the HTTP call (on-prem inference can be slower than cloud APIs).
  • Bearer token auth -- set via MINDROUTER_API_KEY.
Environment Configuration 
# .env — Claude
LLM_PROVIDER=claude
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...

# .env — OpenAI
LLM_PROVIDER=openai
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...

# .env — MindRouter (on-prem)
LLM_PROVIDER=mindrouter
MINDROUTER_API_KEY=mr2_...
MINDROUTER_ENDPOINT_URL=https://mindrouter.uidaho.edu/v1/chat/completions
MINDROUTER_MODEL=moonshotai/kimi-k3

docs.title: Governance and the separate ops classifier
docs.text:
Newsletter prompts include original copy, submitter notes, provided URLs/anchor text, category and staff instructions with active style rules. A repair pass may resend the original prompt, generated draft and findings. Dedicated contact columns are not inserted, but personal information embedded in free text/links is not automatically sanitized. The selected provider is controlled by LLM_PROVIDER; the default configuration is Claude, while deployment examples prefer MindRouter. Provider selection does not establish approved routing.

Event Services uses a separate MindRouter classifier after a harvest. It reads event title, up to 4,000 description characters, location and category, then stores needs, confidence, rationale and staff verdicts. It uses OPS_CLASSIFIER_* with endpoint/key fallbacks to MINDROUTER_*, independent of newsletter provider selection. The content hash tracks assessed source text; per-assessment model and prompt version identifiers are not currently persisted.

See Data governance for the complete sharing/processor inventory and Governance decisions for pending model, gateway, contract and classification approvals. No blanket vendor residency, zero-retention or legal-compliance claim is inferred from the code.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: All endpoints are prefixed with /api/v1. Responses use JSON. Errors return standard { "detail": "..." } bodies.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text:
Public requests carry no credentials. Staff, SLC, and Event Services access reaches the API one of two ways, selected by AUTH_PROVIDER:

  • Session token (AUTH_PROVIDER=oidc): after Microsoft Entra sign-in the backend mints a signed session token; the client sends it as Authorization: Bearer <token>. An invalid or expired token is a 401.
  • Trusted auth boundary (AUTH_PROVIDER=header): the reverse proxy injects X-Trusted-User-Role and X-Trusted-Auth-Secret, and the backend accepts the role only when the secret matches TRUSTED_ROLE_HEADER_SECRET.

Each mode honors only its own credential: under header a bearer token is ignored, and under oidc the X-Trusted-* headers are ignored. Client-supplied X-User-Role is rejected.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text:
Method Path Description GET /api/v1/auth/config { "sso_enabled": bool }. Unauthenticated; the landing page reads it. GET /api/v1/auth/me The signed-in identity { subject, name, role }. Requires a bearer token. GET /api/v1/auth/sso/login Redirects the browser to Microsoft Entra. Optional login_hint=<email> pre-fills Microsoft's form (otherwise the account picker is forced); optional next=<in-app path> is remembered and returned in the callback fragment. oidc only. GET /api/v1/auth/callback Entra reply URL. Mints a session token and redirects to the SPA's /sso/callback with it in the URL fragment (plus next if one was given), or with #error=<reason>. oidc only. GET /api/v1/auth/logout Redirects through Entra's end-session endpoint so both sessions end. oidc only.

Callback error reasons: not_authorized (signed in, but in no mapped App Role), unavailable (directory lookup failed; retry), misconfigured (Graph refused; needs an administrator), no_account (no email claim), sign_in_failed (Entra rejected the exchange).

docs.title: Architecture and production-readiness review — September 18, 2026
docs.text: For editors and product owners, see the plain-language findings and proposed remediation plan.

docs.title: Judgment
docs.text:
The application has a suitable technical foundation and has made real progress, but it is not yet a demonstrated dependable production platform. Repeated feedback exposes weak ownership of editorial content, inconsistent editorial policy, and incomplete verification across the full publishing workflow. The appropriate response is a focused reliability and architecture phase within the existing React/FastAPI/PostgreSQL application.

Keep the modular monolith. Neither a rewrite nor a microservice migration is justified by this review. Traffic capacity is not the immediate problem: preserving an editor's decisions and producing a correct newsletter are.

docs.title: Scope and evidence
docs.text:
• Reviewed the September 15 reports filed as GitHub issues #373–389 and earlier feedback/issue history. Checked current issue states, including previously closed issues covering the same themes.
  • Reviewed local checkout d4d4712 and fetched/reviewed the difference through current origin/main, 7631fbc (September 16). The newer change is the sign-in experience; it does not change the editorial/export findings below.
  • Reviewed repository history beginning February 13, 2026: approximately seven months of development.
  • Inspected nonsecret runtime configuration and style-rule fingerprints in development and production. Both use MindRouter with openai/gpt-oss-120b. Both have all 99 seed rules, active, with text matching the reviewed repository. Neither runtime implements the newer auth_provider setting. Production frontend reports TRUSTED_ROLE_HEADER_ROLE=staff.
  • Reproduced hyperlink loss by generating a DOCX from synthetic linked content and inspecting its XML/relationships: anchor text remained, but no hyperlink element or destination remained.
  • Reproduced selection of older final text by executing the actual version-selection function with two chronological final versions. This proves the selection defect; database row ordering itself is unspecified.
  • All 196 frontend tests in the local checkout passed. Latest main GitHub CI passed. Local backend pytest collection was blocked by a missing installed jwt dependency; no local backend-suite pass is claimed.
  • This was not a live-model quality benchmark, load test, penetration test, restore exercise, or complete infrastructure audit. Missing operational evidence below is not proof that the corresponding infrastructure is absent. No application fixes or deployment changes were made.

docs.title: Are problems recurring?
docs.text:
Yes. Thirteen new issues concern AI editorial behavior; four concern saved content, Jobs output, sorting, and hyperlinks. Earlier issues for most of these themes were closed during July and August. However, distinguish repeated symptoms from proven regressions: a new report can expose an old gap, a different interaction, an undeployed fix, or a changed requirement.

Theme Earlier issues New issues Interpretation Event ordering, complete sentences, acronyms, months #194, #228, #232, #300, #324 #373, #381, #383 Repeated requirements after several correction passes Meaning, audience, recurrence, factual invention #277, #300, #305, #312, #313, #322 #375, #377–380, #382, #385 Related failures to preserve source meaning, with additional protected fact types Headline repeats lead #276 #376 Direct follow-up to an implemented requirement Relative dates and weekday conflicts #306, #325 #374, #384 Recurrence mixed with editorial-policy changes Saved editorial work disappears #64, #193, #198 #386 Persistent ambiguity about which content version is authoritative Jobs treated as articles #197, #281, #299, #304 #387 Repeated mismatch between structured listings and article editing Hyperlinks across editing and publication #202, #227, #309, #326 #389 Repeated integrity failures across representations; export loss is confirmed Earliest actionable date determines ordering #274 #388 New ordering capability, not a demonstrated sorting regression

The July 17 feedback digest already documented original-content loss, repeated style complaints, Jobs requirements, link editing, and scope confusion. These are foundational expectations. The March stakeholder feedback also expected the editor's final text to be the text published.

The currently matching rule databases rule out missing or stale seed text as the current explanation for these reports. They do not prove what prompt/model/configuration was used when each report was filed. Future diagnostic records need that provenance.

docs.title: 1. Editorial authority is distributed across views and copies
docs.text:
The Editor chooses the latest version from a chronologically ordered API result. Builder's _get_best_text instead chooses the first version of the preferred type. The ORM relationship has no defined ordering. Thus the same submission can produce different content depending on which module reads it.

Existing newsletter items also contain copied headline/body text without a source revision identifier. Reassembly deliberately leaves that text alone, protecting manual Builder edits but hiding later upstream corrections. Automatically overwriting all Builder items would introduce another data-loss problem.

AI completion unconditionally sets a submission to ai_edited after waiting for its model call. A human approval during that wait can therefore be superseded by an older operation. Revision checks and explicit transition rules are missing.

Deepening opportunity: concentrate revision selection, staff edits, approval, and edition snapshots in one editorial-content module. Its implementation should own precedence and conflict detection so callers do not reimplement them. Record which revision is approved for which newsletter, and identify edition overrides and upstream changes explicitly. This improves locality and gives tests a meaningful interface: approved content survives every scheduling and publication transition.

Evidence: backend/app/services/newsletter_service.py:361,451; backend/app/models/submission.py:91; backend/app/models/newsletter.py:73; frontend/src/pages/EditPage.tsx:89; backend/app/api/v1/ai_edits.py:147,253,330.

docs.title: 2. Links are content, but their representations are independent
docs.text:
The application uses inline HTML, mutable submission-link rows, editor link arrays, and copied newsletter bodies. These can diverge across revisions. Word export extracts link text and paints it blue/underlined but discards the destination. Git blame shows that implementation dates to the initial February 13 pipeline, rather than a recent regression. Its docstring even claims URLs are appended when the implementation does not do so.

Deepening opportunity: make text and its attached links one versioned content module, with rendering adapters for editor, Builder and DOCX. The test interface must verify destinations and anchor associations in the final artifact, not just whether a preview displays underlining. This also protects job application links.

Evidence: backend/app/utils/export.py:97; backend/app/api/v1/ai_edits.py:340; backend/app/services/ai/editor.py:690; frontend/src/pages/EditPage.tsx:95.

docs.title: 3. Editorial policy has multiple authorities
docs.text:
Database rules, seed JSON, migrations, hard-coded prompts, and deterministic validators all shape the same behavior. For example, the prompt requires a complete event sentence but provides an event-detail fragment as its example. First-person rewriting can substitute an organization name, while new feedback prohibits inventing the speaker.

This is not merely a lack of prompt engineering. The system needs an explicit hierarchy: preserve source facts and editorial intent, apply approved transformations, enforce mechanically checkable formatting, and flag unresolved ambiguity.

The pipeline has already evolved usefully: it performs deterministic checks, a bounded repair attempt, and reports remaining findings. Existing production-derived fixtures test bad output, successful repair, provider failure, and a stubborn model. Those are valuable tests, but their providers return prescribed answers. They do not establish that the actual deployed model follows the full editorial policy.

Deepening opportunity: concentrate policy precedence and validation in an editorial-policy module; retain the real provider seam and its multiple adapters. Record rule/prompt/model versions, then maintain a reviewed evaluation set measuring factual preservation, dates, links, audience, Jobs formatting, and editing effort. Run model evaluations separately from deterministic unit tests and compare releases on the same cases.

Evidence: backend/app/services/ai/prompts.py:62,75,94; backend/app/services/ai/editor.py:549; backend/tests/test_issue_300_production_fixtures.py:20,138.

docs.title: 4. Content dates and publication dates need separate meanings
docs.text:
The prompt refers to publication date without receiving explicit publication/current-date/timezone context in its user prompt. Validators use date.today(). Upcoming event dates, registration deadlines, publication schedules, and recurring occurrences are different domain facts; prose alone is an unreliable basis for sorting them.

Three decisions should precede implementation:

Deepening opportunity: give verified content facts and publication scheduling separate ownership. Treat article copy, structured Jobs listings and imported calendar entries as distinct content types with shared publication mechanisms. Do not infer newsletter audience eligibility from the publication channel.

Evidence: backend/app/services/ai/prompts.py:86,127; backend/app/services/ai/editor.py:490,557; backend/app/models/submission.py:61; backend/app/services/newsletter_service.py:319,375.

docs.title: 374 requests replacing relative dates; #325 requests preserving both relative wording and explicit dates. Define reference date, timezone, and source precedence.
384 requests preserving contradictory source weekday/date values for staff review. Distinguish this from deriving a missing weekday from a known date under #306.
387 requests visible job titles, while #299 intentionally removes a separate published headline. Editor visibility and published formatting need distinct rules.
What has evolved correctly
docs.text:
• The React/FastAPI/PostgreSQL architecture fits the workload and remains understandable.
  • Provider adapters provide a useful seam with multiple actual implementations.
  • Original content is preserved on finalization; final text and approval status are saved together.
  • Seeding no longer overwrites staff-edited rules by default, addressing the earlier #195 failure.
  • Imported Jobs have deterministic structured formatting.
  • Alembic migrations, migration-drift CI, PostgreSQL smoke checks, server-side role dependencies, upload validation and frontend workflow tests are substantial improvements.

The problem is incomplete consolidation around the domain rules those improvements revealed. Moving more functions into files would not by itself fix this. A deep module earns its place by keeping an important rule consistent across callers.

docs.title: Production dependability and scale
docs.text:
Authentication requires a verified deployment, not just merged code. Production currently stamps staff at the proxy and lacks the newer SSO configuration. This establishes no application-level distinction between individual visitors reaching that proxy; upstream network restrictions were not audited. Before an SSO rollout, address two code-derived hazards: bearer tokens are accepted in header mode even though startup checks for signing-secret strength and the default secret are skipped there, and trusted-header roles remain accepted in OIDC mode. JWT signature verification still runs, but the public default signing secret makes the first combination unsafe. That is a repository deployment hazard, not a claim of an active exploit against the older production runtime.

AI work is process-local. The job dictionary, semaphore, and FastAPI background tasks lose state on restart and do not work reliably across multiple workers. Results have no eviction. Persist job state, bound the backlog, recover interrupted work, and check the input revision before applying results. A small durable worker arrangement is sufficient; a broad distributed architecture is unnecessary.

CI does not yet enforce the strongest available tests. The frontend CI job lints and builds but never runs Vitest. Backend tests primarily use SQLite; PostgreSQL CI verifies migrations and performs smoke checks. Add frontend tests to CI, then a few complete submission-to-DOCX and concurrent-edit scenarios. Green CI is useful evidence within its actual scope.

Operations need proof. Backup and recovery documentation gives useful procedures and target RTO/RPO values, but this review did not verify a successful restore, alert delivery, or named operational coverage. Reconsider whether losing 24 hours of submissions or waiting four hours near a publication deadline is acceptable. Feedback notifications are still disabled in production.

Builds and capacity need bounded improvements. Backend dependencies have lower bounds without a resolved lockfile; rebuilding an old commit can change its dependencies. Record deployed commit, immutable image, schema revision and policy version. Some filtering/assembly loads broad candidate sets and eagerly fetches edit history; measure with realistic retained history and optimize those paths. No current load result justifies a claim that the system is slow, or that a new database/stack is needed.

Evidence: backend/app/api/deps.py:26,73,76; backend/app/config.py:153; backend/app/auth/session_tokens.py:35; backend/app/api/v1/ai_edits.py:51,228; .github/workflows/ci.yml:72; backend/tests/conftest.py:19; backend/pyproject.toml:6; backend/app/services/submission_service.py:186; docs/backup-and-recovery.md.

docs.title: Documentation and scope
docs.text:
Documentation is substantial but not a reliable current domain map. The architecture service inventory omits several newer systems. It still describes a Compose database container although PostgreSQL is external. README says 37 seeded rules; the actual count is 99. PRODUCT.md lists three audiences and omits Ops. There is no CONTEXT.md and only one ADR, for authentication.

The application now covers newsletter production, leadership-calendar intelligence, and event-services triage/classification. These can remain in one deployment, but should have explicit owners, vocabularies, access rules, and module interfaces. Their expansion does not establish that the core newsletter workflow is ready. The earlier feedback already questioned SLC/calendar scope.

Update documentation around source submission, AI draft, staff working revision, approval, edition snapshot, actionable date, audience versus channel, standing policy, and feedback disposition. Record the contentious decisions, rather than relying on successive issue bodies to define the product.

docs.title: Recommended sequence and release evidence
docs.text:
1. Protect editorial work and access first: fix final-version selection and real DOCX links; resolve authentication defaults and verify the deployment cutover. Preserve a manual editorial path when AI is unavailable.
  2. Consolidate content ownership: explicit revisions, approval transitions, link snapshots, conflict checks, edition overrides and upstream-change indication. Use #386/#389 as end-to-end acceptance cases.
  3. Resolve policy and evaluate: agree date and Jobs semantics; consolidate contradictory instructions; benchmark the deployed model against reviewed source-fidelity cases. Treat #373–385 as one policy/evaluation programme with individually traceable reports.
  4. Make release and recovery repeatable: durable AI jobs, frontend CI, PostgreSQL workflow checks, immutable releases, actual restore/alert exercises, and deployment fingerprints.
  5. Refresh domain documentation and scope: establish ownership of newsletter, SLC and Ops modules; stage additional expansion against evidence that the core workflow is dependable.

Before calling the application dependable production, demonstrate that two editors cannot silently overwrite each other; a restart does not lose AI job state; the selected approved revision reaches Builder and Word unchanged except for deliberate edition edits; every published link retains its destination; anonymous/SLC/Ops/staff access behaves correctly; and a real backup restores within an editorially acceptable deadline. Close the feedback loop with editor acceptance on the deployed build, recording report → issue → implementation → deployment → retest.

docs.title: Three-Tier Architecture
docs.text:
The application follows a standard three-tier design:

React SPA (Vite)  --->  FastAPI REST API  --->  SQLite / PostgreSQL
   Port 5173               Port 8001              File / TCP
  • Presentation -- React single-page application served by Vite in development and nginx in production. Communicates exclusively through the REST API. Styled with Tailwind CSS v4 using University of Idaho brand tokens (see Branding).
  • Application -- FastAPI backend providing versioned endpoints under /api/v1/. All business logic lives in service modules.
  • Data -- SQLAlchemy async ORM with SQLite for local development and PostgreSQL for production. Alembic manages schema migrations.

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
The primary data pipeline moves a submission from intake through AI editing to final newsletter export:

Contributor submits announcement

        v
  Submission record created (with Links, ScheduleRequests)

        v
  AI Edit Pipeline triggered

        |  - Construct LLM prompt

        |  - Post-process (headline case, diff)

  Newsletter assembled (submissions, recurring messages, and imported external items placed in sections, reordered)

docs.text:

docs.title: LLM Abstraction
docs.text:
The AI layer uses a provider factory pattern so the LLM backend can be switched via environment variable:

# .env
LLM_PROVIDER=mindrouter   # or "claude" or "openai"

Each provider implements the LLMProvider abstract base class (complete and complete_json methods), and the factory instantiates the correct adapter at startup. This keeps route handlers and the editing pipeline independent of any specific LLM vendor.

See AI Editing for full details on the provider interface and MindRouter specifics.

docs.title: Audit logging and monitoring
docs.text: Reviewed October 22, 2026. The code provides minimized operational diagnostics; it does not yet provide a complete per-user data-access or mutation audit trail. Editorial versions record copy provenance, not every access or actor action.

docs.title: Implemented logging controls
docs.text:
• Application sign-in messages record outcome and mapped role, never subject, name, group list, tokens or authorization-code parameters.
  • Link unwrapping records only the wrapper type, never full URLs, query strings, paths, fragments or extracted destinations.
  • AI/ops and feedback failure messages use exception class names, opaque application record IDs where useful, and fixed event text. Provider messages, response bodies and traceback text are excluded. Feedback delivery failures persist the error class rather than the transport's arbitrary message.
  • Docker uvicorn uses backend/logging.json, JSON formatting and no request access log. The formatter excludes exception messages/tracebacks; call sites remain responsible for minimizing event arguments. HTTP client DEBUG/INFO URL logging is disabled by that configuration.
  • Frontend nginx access logs contain timestamp, HTTP method, status, byte count and duration. They omit request URI/query, Referer, user agent and client IP. Its error threshold is crit because ordinary error diagnostics can contain the original request line. Rare critical diagnostics and campus ingress logs still require restricted access and deployment review.
  • Compose limits each application container's json-file logs to three files of 10 MB. This bounds size; it is not time-based retention or aggregation.

For local servers use the same settings when handling anything beyond synthetic inputs (from backend/):

uvicorn app.main:app --port 8001 --reload --no-access-log --log-config logging.json

Never enable HTTP/SDK wire-debug logging on real content. Avoid secrets, contact values, raw copy, links, prompts, completions, browser context and untrusted input in log arguments. Exception classes are useful diagnostics; deeper investigation must use an approved restricted process with deliberately minimized captures.

docs.title: Planned audit-event contract
docs.text:
Event family Allowlisted fields Not implemented yet Submission access/change and deletion Event code, opaque record ID, actor reference approved by privacy review, changed field names, time Consistent event emission and actor mapping AI edit/classification Event code, record ID, approved provider/model identifier, duration, counts, outcome Uniform success/failure and model-call audit events Publication/export Event code, issue ID, operation, actor reference, time Export/access review trail Configuration and deployment Event code, revision/digest, field names, actor reference, outcome Change/deploy event store and review Authorization failures Fixed reason code, route template, mapped role, time Central security event stream and alerts

Do not log user-supplied field values or client identity headers. A per-user audit identifier requires a Data Owner/security decision; do not quietly reintroduce email addresses to implement traceability. Hashes of emails are still linkable identifiers and require review.

docs.title: Retention and operations evidence
docs.text:
Proposed general-log retention is 90 days; proposed security/error retention is one year. Both require approved classification, access and expiry rules. No central destination, retention execution, alerting, integrity/immutability or reviewer is verified by repository configuration. Complete those fields in Governance decisions before claiming the targets operate. Treat existing logs from earlier releases as potentially containing personal data and sensitive URLs; restrict access and review expiry with the data owner.

The backend Compose healthcheck already queries /api/v1/readyz. Use /health for liveness and /readyz for DB/reference-data readiness; keep staff workflow smoke tests separate. See Backup and recovery.

Regression checks exercise successful/refused/failed sign-in, provider failures, wrapped links and exception formatting with synthetic sensitive markers. Review logging call sites and ingress configuration whenever identity, AI, export or transport code changes. Record a deployed log sample and retention validation without collecting personal data as proof.

docs.title: Backup, recovery and incident response
docs.text: Reviewed October 22, 2026. This is an operating procedure, not proof that jobs are installed or that a recovery target was achieved. Record installation, access/encryption controls, latest successful backup and measured restore results in Governance decisions. Proposed RPO: 24 hours; proposed RTO: four hours. Both require a restore exercise.

docs.title: Topology and protected copies
docs.text:
Compose contains frontend nginx and backend uvicorn. PostgreSQL is external on insight-db-net; application uploads are in the uploads volume. Identify the actual volume with docker volume inspect/Compose configuration rather than assuming its name. Environment files contain secrets and require separately controlled encrypted backups. Source recovery comes from the repository plus release/image metadata.

Treat all DB/upload backups as containing personal information. Keep encrypted, access-controlled off-host copies and separate keys. Never copy real backups into ordinary development, CI or an unapproved test environment.

docs.title: Paired, versioned backup procedure
docs.text:
Run this procedure from an approved backup agent with credentials supplied outside command history. Configure service files or a managed credential mechanism for PostgreSQL; do not put passwords in a command line. Confirm source DB identity and the upload source mount before every installation.

  1. Pause application writes (stop backend or enable an upstream maintenance page) while taking the pair. Merely starting a DB dump and rsync at different times does not guarantee consistency between referenced uploads and database rows.
  2. Create a new restricted timestamped directory, e.g. /backups/ucmnews/prod/2026-10-22T020000Z/, using umask 077 and a directory name that is never reused. Keep prod and dev separate.
  3. Run pg_dump --format=custom --file=<new-directory>/database.dump <service-db>. Copy the upload volume into <new-directory>/uploads/ with rsync -a. Neither command should overwrite the previous recovery point.
  4. Record the backup timestamp, database identity, application commit/image digests, Alembic revision, upload volume identity, file count and checksums in a restricted manifest. Do not include secrets. Confirm both operations succeeded before declaring a recovery point complete and resuming writes.
  5. Encrypt/replicate the pair to the approved off-host store, verify checksums, and record success/failure and alert destination. Encrypt environment-file backups separately; protect encryption keys away from the backup data.

The earlier single-directory rsync example is retired: it neither preserved historical upload snapshots nor expired deleted files. For larger datasets use a reviewed snapshot/consistent online backup design rather than extending downtime without agreement.

Proposed tiers are daily 30 days, weekly 90 days and monthly one year. Until the Data Owner approves them they are planning values. Implement tier labels and expiry on complete recovery-point directories/pairs, not ad hoc removal of files inside them. A retained weekly/monthly pair can outlive the daily tier. Holds and backup retention extensions require recorded owner authorization. Monitor failed backups, missing pairs, off-host replication and expiry failures.

docs.title: Restore exercise and data loss
docs.text:
Use an isolated, approved recovery environment for a monthly exercise and before significant schema/storage changes. Disable public ingress and outbound AI or feedback work; never expose the restored DB through the normal dev host. Protect real restore data with production controls and teardown after verification.

  1. Preserve current database/uploads and failure evidence before any replacement. Do not start with dropdb against the affected production database.
  2. Select a complete, verified DB/upload pair and its matching release. Restore the dump to a new isolated database. pg_restore --list only checks archive readability; it does not demonstrate a usable restore.
  3. Restore uploads into a new volume/directory. Verify checksums and DB image references. Set correct ownership; do not copy over a live volume blindly.
  4. Start the matching application release with migrations reviewed for that exact source/target revision. Prevent the normal entrypoint from automatically migrating to a different revision before compatibility has been checked.
  5. Verify schema revision, record counts, issue snapshots and provenance, reference data, uploaded-image readability, role isolation, and a synthetic create/edit/export cycle. Use approved credentials for staff tests. Verify disposed/held data handling before reconnecting restored data to users.
  6. Record measured data loss and recovery duration, backup/release revisions, tests, reviewer, deviations and corrective work. Cut traffic over only after owner acceptance. Securely remove test copies and temporary credentials.

A restore record must include the actual date/operator, pair identifier, checksum results, expected/actual RPO and RTO, checks passed/failed, decision and teardown. No completed exercise is claimed by this repository update.

docs.title: Container recovery and release rollback
docs.text:
For a stateless container failure, inspect docker compose -p ucmnews-prod ps and minimized logs, then restart the failed service. Rebuilding is a release operation, because the backend entrypoint runs Alembic and seeds data.

For a bad deployment:

  1. Pause writes/traffic as needed; capture the deployed commit/image digests and current Alembic revision, then create a fresh paired recovery point.
  2. Compare the current and target migration chains before starting the older release. Check whether the previous code can run on the current schema.
  3. If compatible, deploy the known-good immutable image/revision and verify. If incompatible, prefer a forward fix or restore a paired backup into a new DB/volume. A downgrade is permitted only after reviewing and testing that exact migration path, data-loss implications and rollback plan on an isolated copy. Never assume alembic downgrade -1 reverses an entire release.
  4. Recheck health, readiness, role-specific workflows and source/archive integrity before reopening traffic. Record the result and any data loss.

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text:
Run against the relevant host (prod shown):

curl --fail --silent --show-error https://ucmnews.insight.uidaho.edu/api/v1/health
curl --fail --silent --show-error https://ucmnews.insight.uidaho.edu/api/v1/readyz

/health checks process liveness only. /readyz executes database queries and checks load-bearing reference tables; it does not prove every workflow is healthy. Importing the engine does not test connectivity. /settings/ai is currently public metadata, not a database health probe. Inspect backup success daily; check disk/capacity and log rotation weekly; perform and record restore exercises monthly. The backend Compose healthcheck already uses /readyz.

docs.title: Incident response
docs.text:
Severity Working response target Examples Critical Immediate, within one hour Suspected data breach, data loss, complete outage High Within four hours Editorial pipeline/export unavailable Medium Within one business day Degraded import or performance Low Within one week Minor display or documentation problem

These are proposed support targets pending named owner acceptance. Contact the technical/operations owner and UCM sponsor through the established escalation process; security incidents also go to the University's Information Security Office. See repository SECURITY.md for the reporting process; do not include raw personal data in ordinary issue reports.

Detect → triage → contain → notify authorized responders → preserve minimized evidence → repair/restore → verify → review. For High/Critical incidents record a restricted timeline, impact, affected systems, containment, root cause, measured recovery, decision owner and prevention work. Named on-call coverage and verified contact references remain in the governance decision register.

docs.title: Shared button accessibility baseline, version 1.1
docs.text:
Updated October 26, 2026 for #248. Brand provenance remains the University of Idaho Brand Book 2023; the existing token values are unchanged. Engineering maintains this control implementation through repository review. This does not assign institutional Data Owner or accessibility approval.

Enabled shared-button pairing Contrast ratio Supported use ui-black on ui-gold-500 6.83:1 Primary action text ui-black on ui-gold-600 5.18:1 Primary hover text White on status-success-800 7.68:1 Success action text; hover darkens the background

Ratios use sRGB relative luminance from the actual theme hex values; enabled normal-size text requires at least 4.5:1. Disabled controls retain native disabled semantics and reduced opacity; these ratios describe enabled controls.

Shared buttons expose native names, disabled and pressed states and keyboard activation. A two-pixel dark focus outline with a two-pixel offset is intended for light surfaces, including confirmation dialogs. Reduced-motion preference removes color transitions. Dark-surface use requires a contrasting focus treatment and separate verification. Tests cover contrast from theme values, keyboard activation and disabled behavior; these checks do not establish full app conformance.

Version 1.1 replaces failing white/gold and white/mid-green pairings and adds an explicit shared-button focus treatment. Remaining #248 work includes raw page buttons, selected segmented controls, links, form controls, toggles and navigation, all status pairings, browser/forced-colors checks and broader token documentation.

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository and follow the Deployment guide to set up backend and frontend environments.
  2. Install backend with pip install -e ".[dev]" (includes test and lint tools).
  3. Apply migrations with alembic upgrade head, then seed the database with python -m app.db.seed.
  4. Verify both servers start cleanly before making changes.

docs.title: Database Columns
docs.text:
All SQLAlchemy column names use PascalCase_With_Underscores:

# Correct
Original_Headline = sa.Column(sa.Text, nullable=False)
Created_At = sa.Column(sa.DateTime, server_default=sa.func.now())

# Incorrect
original_headline = sa.Column(sa.Text, nullable=False)
created_at = sa.Column(sa.DateTime, server_default=sa.func.now())

docs.title: SQLAlchemy Imports
docs.text:
Import SQLAlchemy as sa and use the alias throughout:

import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship

docs.title: Relationship Loading
docs.text:
Use lazy="selectin" for all relationships to avoid N+1 queries in async contexts:

links = relationship("SubmissionLink", back_populates="submission", lazy="selectin")

docs.title: Docstrings
docs.text:
All public functions, classes, and modules require docstrings. Use Google-style format:

async def get_submission(db: AsyncSession, submission_id: UUID) -> Submission:
    """Fetch a single submission by ID.

    Args:
        db: Active database session.
        submission_id: UUID of the submission to retrieve.

    Returns:
        The Submission object.

    Raises:
        HTTPException: 404 if submission not found.
    """

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
• Components use TypeScript with explicit prop interfaces.
  • Styling uses TailwindCSS v4 utility classes with University of Idaho brand tokens (see Branding).
  • API calls go through dedicated client functions in src/api/.

docs.title: AllowedValue Pattern
docs.text:
When introducing a new categorical field, follow the AllowedValue pattern instead of hardcoding options:

  1. Add a new value group in backend/data/allowed_values/allowed_values.json (e.g., Priority_Level).
  2. Insert rows with Value_Group, Code, Label, Display_Order, Visibility_Role, and Description where applicable.
  3. Reference the group in forms via GET /api/v1/allowed-values?group=Priority_Level.
  4. Validate against allowed values in the service layer.

This keeps all categorical data in the database and makes it editable without code changes.

docs.title: Branching and Pull Requests
docs.text:
1. Create a feature branch from main: 
    git checkout -b feature/short-description
  2. Make focused commits with clear messages.
  3. Run tests before opening a PR: 
    cd backend && source .venv/bin/activate
pytest
  4. Open a pull request against main with a description of what changed and why.
  5. Address review feedback in additional commits (do not force-push over review comments).

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
cd backend
source .venv/bin/activate
pytest                     # all tests
pytest tests/test_api/     # API tests only
pytest -x                  # stop on first failure
pytest --cov=app           # with coverage report

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
cd frontend
npm test

Test Database

Tests use an in-memory SQLite database by default. No setup is required beyond installing dependencies.

Production runs PostgreSQL, which enforces foreign keys and stores timestamps differently, so CI also runs the whole suite against PostgreSQL. To do the same locally, point TEST_DATABASE_URL at an empty database (the suite creates and drops every table):

docker run -d --rm --name ucm-test-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pg -e POSTGRES_DB=ucmnews_test -p 55433:5432 postgres:16-alpine
TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://postgres:pg@127.0.0.1:55433/ucmnews_test pytest

docs.title: Adding a New API Resource
docs.text:
When adding a new resource (e.g., Comment):

  1. Create the SQLAlchemy model in backend/app/models/.
  2. Create Pydantic schemas in backend/app/schemas/.
  3. Create a service module in backend/app/services/.
  4. Create a route module in backend/app/api/v1/.
  5. Register the router in backend/app/api/v1/router.py.
  6. Generate an Alembic migration: alembic revision --autogenerate -m "add comments".
  7. Write tests covering CRUD operations and edge cases.

docs.title: Data governance and privacy
docs.text: Reviewed against repository code on October 22, 2026. This describes the implemented application; it does not attest to live production configuration or institutional approval. Accountable people and approval references are tracked in Governance decisions.

docs.title: Data inventory and classification
docs.text:
The data dictionary inventories every ORM table and column. Its machine-readable source also drives the staff governance page. Classification is provisional until the Data Owner and institutional reviewers approve the mapping to APM 30.11; local labels are not institutional approval.

Local handling label Working definition Examples Public Reviewed content approved for public release, or public reference data Published issue copy, public calendar feed, category labels Internal Working or operational data available to authorized roles Unpublished copy, SLC-only event details, ops verdicts, AI provenance Confidential Contact information, free text with incidental personal information, or credentials Submitter/contact email, notes, feedback details, identity claims, session tokens Restricted Placeholder for information requiring additional institutional controls No intentional collection; unexpected sensitive content needs incident review

Unpublished content is not classified Public solely because it may later be published. Treat mixed datasets and generated output according to the most sensitive content present. Free-text fields, links, JSON flags, and images can contain information beyond their intended purpose.

docs.title: Personal and authentication data
docs.text:

reported role is client context, not verified identity Email/username subject, display name, mapped role Entra/Graph exchange; signed app JWT; browser localStorage Sign-in and authorization JWT defaults to 480 minutes; browser token removed on local sign-out or next load detecting expiry OIDC state and next-path context Signed browser session cookie; transient server memory Bind authorization flow to browser Starlette session cookie defaults to 14 days; verify cookie policy during deployment review Entra tokens/group claims Transient backend memory during sign-in Validate identity; optionally query Graph /me/memberOf Not intentionally stored as database records or forwarded to the SPA API keys, DB credentials, signing/client secrets Runtime environment and deployment secret files Backend/provider access Rotate per owner-approved secrets procedure; never submit in forms

There is no user table. This does not mean identity data is absent or that nothing is persisted: the browser stores the app JWT, including identifiable claims. JWT expiry ends authorization; it does not remotely erase localStorage on an inactive browser. Signed cookies and JWTs are not encrypted storage.

The app does not intentionally request student IDs, education records, health or financial records, passwords, or government identifiers. Free text and uploads can still contain them. FERPA scope and directory-information treatment require institutional privacy review; no categorical legal conclusion is asserted here. If unexpected protected content is found, stop further sharing and follow the incident procedure below.

docs.title: Authentication and authorization
docs.text:
AUTH_PROVIDER=oidc uses Entra's confidential-client authorization-code flow. The backend verifies the response, maps App Roles (or Graph groups), and issues an HS256 app JWT. Only bearer credentials count in this mode. Unmapped users are refused; role changes take effect at next sign-in or token expiry. Browser sign-out clears local state and goes through Entra logout. There is no per-token revocation service.

AUTH_PROVIDER=header accepts X-Trusted-User-Role only with the configured X-Trusted-Auth-Secret. Bearer tokens do not grant access in this mode. X-User-Role is rejected. The frontend proxy overwrites trusted headers. If the proxy asserts staff for every request, everyone who can reach it receives staff access. This is a prototype boundary, not evidence of individual sign-in. Production should use OIDC; verify actual enablement separately for each host. See Deployment and ADR-001.

All paths below are under /api/v1. Public means no identity credential is required; it does not imply that every column in a response is approved for publication.

Dataset / route family Public SLC Ops Staff POST /submissions/ Create with permitted public category; receives own created response Create with permitted category Create with permitted category Create with permitted category /submissions/ list/detail, updates, links, schedules, images, deletes No No general access No Read/change/delete GET /submissions/?slc_calendar_only=true No Read; dedicated submitter name/email/notes and editorial fields redacted No Read including staff fields /slc/harvest, /slc/harvested-events and triage/acknowledgment No Read, harvest, change SLC review; flagging creates SLC-only submission No Same /ops/harvested-events and needs/verdicts/acknowledgment No No Read, change ops review; add/remove staff-origin needs; confirm/reject AI needs Same /ai-edits, /newsletters including imports/exports, /recurring-messages, /style-rules No No No Read/change according to endpoint POST /feedback Create; receives created record Same Same Same Feedback list/summary/update, notification retry, GitHub export preparation No No No Yes Allowed values, sections, schedule GETs, /settings/ai Read; category visibility filtering applies to allowed values Read Read Read Schedule POST/DELETE No No No Yes /health, /readyz, /auth/config Read Read Read Read /auth/me No Own valid bearer identity in OIDC mode Same Same

SLC redaction removes dedicated contact fields, not names/emails embedded in event copy or links. Staff inherit both triage capabilities; SLC and ops are separate roles. Current settings/sections/schedule read endpoints are public; they must contain no secrets. API responses, permission tests, and the API reference are the implementation evidence.

docs.title: Data flows and external processing
docs.text:
1. A public or authorized caller submits copy, contact fields, notes, links and dates through React → nginx → FastAPI → database. Staff can upload an image.
  2. Staff trigger newsletter editing. Active DB style rules form the system prompt. The user prompt contains headline/body, category, submitter notes, provided links including URLs/parameters, and editor instructions. A compliance repair request can resend the original input, generated draft and deterministic findings. Dedicated submitter name/email, assignment, and editorial notes columns are not explicitly inserted, but personal data in content is not automatically sanitized. Returned copy, flags, change summaries, model/provider and editor instructions may persist in edit history.
  3. Trumba calendar pages/feed and PeopleAdmin postings are fetched on demand. SLC harvesting upserts structured JSON-feed occurrences in harvested_events. SLC flagging promotes an event into a submission and records its provenance.
  4. A harvest queues ops classification in the background. A separate MindRouter provider receives title, description (up to 4,000 characters), location and category. It uses OPS_CLASSIFIER_*, with endpoint/key falling back to MINDROUTER_*; it is independent of LLM_PROVIDER. Needs/confidence/rationale and staff verdicts persist. Rationale may quote source text. Staff judgments survive reassessment; assessment content hashes identify source versions.
  5. Approved submissions and external/recurring items become issue snapshots. Staff download Word exports. Dedicated contact columns and internal metadata are not automatically exported, but contact text intentionally in copy remains.
  6. Feedback stores submitted free text and lightweight browser context. Its notifier is disabled. Staff may prepare GitHub Markdown containing report details and context; review/redact before opening or publishing a GitHub issue, including the URL prefill sent to GitHub. No automatic external delivery is enabled. Future notifier payloads can contain summary and optional contact email and require destination approval.
Processor Configured use Evidence required before an institutional assurance Anthropic / OpenAI Selected newsletter editor; local default is Claude Approved processor/model, endpoint and account configuration, contract retention/training/residency terms, external sharing authorization MindRouter Optional newsletter editor; dedicated ops classifier Approved endpoint/model and operating controls; configurable URLs alone do not prove campus-only routing Microsoft Entra / Graph Sign-in and optional group lookup Registration/consent, scopes, role assignments, secret ownership and rotation Trumba / PeopleAdmin Public source reads Source purpose, endpoint inventory and operational limits GitHub Source control and optional staff-prepared feedback export Approved access and export review; protected data excluded

No external-provider residency or zero-retention claim follows from source code. No-training terms, where agreed, do not imply zero retention. Processor approval references remain pending in the decision register. See AI editing.

docs.title: Uploads and minimization
docs.text:
JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP uploads are UUID-named in the upload volume. Supported still images are decoded and rewritten without metadata; processing failure rejects the upload. GIF does not receive the same EXIF rewrite. Image content can itself identify people. Deleting a submission through the existing endpoint does not currently guarantee upload-file disposal; use the reviewed disposal design rather than claiming endpoint deletion meets retention policy.

Do not put protected records or credentials in content, links, notes or feedback. Review free text before AI processing/publication/export. Automated PII detection and source-wide sanitization are not implemented and would not guarantee removal.

docs.title: Retention, logging and ownership
docs.text:
Retention and disposal distinguishes proposed periods from enforced behavior, documents source/archive dependencies, and provides a read-only inventory command. No automatic purge is enabled. The Data Owner must resolve periods, holds and academic-year boundaries before destructive scheduling.

Audit logging specifies minimized diagnostics, Docker limits, remaining access-audit work, and unverified aggregation/retention targets. Backup and recovery describes versioned backup and release-specific recovery procedures; job installation and restore proof remain operational evidence to collect.

The decision register records accountable-role vacancies, classification, processor, dev/test, tooling and approval decisions. Never treat a blank approval reference as approval. Schema changes must update ORM, migrations, API/types, catalog, vocabulary baseline and docs in the same review; run the repository governance check before merging.

docs.title: Incident handling
docs.text: If protected or unexpectedly sensitive content is exposed or submitted, pause further AI/export/publication, restrict access, preserve minimized evidence and notify the University Information Security Office through the established campus process. Coordinate with the technical owner and UCM; do not copy the content into GitHub, chat or email during investigation. Determine scope, containment and any notification obligation with authorized institutional responders. Use the recovery runbook for service restoration and record a post-incident review.

docs.title: Data Model
docs.text:
This document describes the current SQLAlchemy ORM surface for the UCM Daily Register application. It is intended to be the human-readable schema inventory for engineers, data stewards, and governance reviewers.

Source of truth

The SQLAlchemy models in backend/app/models/ define the application schema. Alembic migrations define reproducible schema evolution. Seed JSON under backend/data/ defines bootstrap reference data, not the expected contents of long-lived dev or production databases.

docs.title: Portfolio Naming Convention
docs.text:
UCM follows the UI Insight / AI4RA-UDM column naming convention: PascalCase_With_Underscores, such as Target_Newsletter, Created_At, and Submission_Id.

The application intentionally differs from OpenERA in two ways:

  • Table names are lowercase plural, such as submissions and newsletters.
  • Primary keys are UUID strings named Id rather than UDM-style {Entity}_ID columns.

These differences are documented in the UDM alignment report and should be treated as legacy application conventions, not the preferred pattern for new governed applications.

docs.title: Entity Overview
docs.text:
Area Tables Purpose Controlled vocabularies allowed_values Database-backed pick lists and status/type codes Submission intake submissions, submission_links, submission_schedule_requests Public and staff-submitted newsletter content, links, and requested run dates Editorial history edit_versions Immutable original, AI-suggested, and editor-final snapshots Newsletter assembly newsletters, newsletter_items, newsletter_external_items, newsletter_sections Dated issues, section placement, and imported calendar/job items Recurring editorial content recurring_messages, recurring_message_issue_overrides Staff-managed reusable copy and issue-level skip overrides Publication schedule schedule_configs, blackout_dates, schedule_mode_overrides, custom_publish_dates Academic-year, summer, winter-break, blackout, and ad hoc publish rules AI editing policy style_rules Database-managed editorial rules injected into LLM prompts

The current ORM surface has 19 tables. The generated data dictionary validates every column against model declarations and is the complete inventory; the sections below explain the main relationships.

allowed_values, style_rules, and the schedule reference tables are joined by code conventions rather than database foreign keys. For example, submissions.Category references allowed_values where Value_Group = 'Submission_Category'.

docs.title: allowed_values
docs.text:
Central controlled vocabulary table for category, type, status, severity, and schedule-mode values.

Column Notes Id UUID string primary key Value_Group Vocabulary group, such as Submission_Status Code Machine-readable value code Label Human-readable UI label Display_Order Ordering for dropdowns and settings pages Is_Active Soft-disable flag Visibility_Role public or staff, used for submitter category filtering Description Optional steward-facing description

Unique constraint: (Value_Group, Code).

docs.title: submissions
docs.text:
Core content-intake entity. A submission stores the original headline/body, submitter contact data, editorial workflow fields, optional image reference, and current workflow status.

Column Notes Category AllowedValue group Submission_Category Target_Newsletter AllowedValue group Target_Newsletter Original_Headline, Original_Body Submitted content Submitter_Name, Submitter_Email PII used for editorial contact Submitter_Notes Free-text instructions; may contain incidental PII Assigned_Editor, Editorial_Notes Staff-only editorial fields in API responses Has_Image, Image_Path Uploaded image flag and UUID filename Survey_End_Date Optional date used for survey handling Status AllowedValue group Submission_Status Show_In_SLC_Calendar Staff/SLC visibility flag for leadership event review Event_Classification Strategic or signature event label for the SLC calendar Approved_Version_Id FK to edit_versions.Id: the exact revision staff approved; cleared when a later draft is saved Created_At, Updated_At Server timestamps

Relationships: has many submission_links, submission_schedule_requests, and edit_versions; can be placed in many newsletter_items.

docs.text:
Hyperlinks associated with a submission.

Column Notes Submission_Id FK to submissions.Id Url Destination URL Anchor_Text Optional display text Display_Order Link ordering within the submission

docs.title: submission_schedule_requests
docs.text:
Requested publication dates and recurrence preferences for a submission.

Column Notes Submission_Id FK to submissions.Id Requested_Date Primary requested publication date Second_Requested_Date Secondary date, used when Target_Newsletter = both Repeat_Count, Repeat_Note Legacy repeat-run metadata Is_Flexible, Flexible_Deadline Submitter flexibility metadata Recurrence_Type, Recurrence_Interval, Recurrence_End_Date Staff recurrence rules Excluded_Dates JSON list of skipped or rescheduled occurrences

docs.title: edit_versions
docs.text:
Append-only editorial snapshots. The application creates an original version and one or more ai_suggested or editor_final versions rather than rewriting previous content in place.

Which revision is authoritative is decided only in app/services/editorial_content.py: the approved revision (submissions.Approved_Version_Id), else the newest staff final, else the newest AI suggestion, else the original. Timestamps never decide approval.

Column Notes Submission_Id FK to submissions.Id Version_Type AllowedValue group Version_Type Headline, Body Text snapshot at this editing stage Headline_Case AllowedValue group Headline_Case Flags JSON list of AI/rule findings for editor review Changes_Made JSON list of substantive changes AI_Provider, AI_Model Provider and model used for AI-generated versions Editor_Instructions Staff instruction text for the edit; may contain incidental personal information Created_At Immutable creation timestamp, set by the application to the microsecond

docs.text:
A dated edition of The Daily Register or My UI.

Column Notes Newsletter_Type AllowedValue group Newsletter_Type Publish_Date Issue date Status AllowedValue group Newsletter_Status Created_At, Updated_At Server timestamps

Unique constraint: (Newsletter_Type, Publish_Date).

docs.title: newsletter_items
docs.text:
Placement of a submission into a newsletter issue and section.

Column Notes Newsletter_Id FK to newsletters.Id Submission_Id FK to submissions.Id Section_Id FK to newsletter_sections.Id Position Ordering within a section Final_Headline, Final_Body Copy as placed in the issue Run_Number Which run of the item this placement represents Manually_Placed Staff changed section placement; reassembly preserves it Source_Version_Id FK to edit_versions.Id: the revision the copy was taken from; empty for hand-added items and items assembled before tracking Edition_Edited Staff changed this item's copy in the Builder; reassembly never overwrites it Upstream_Reviewed_Version_Id FK to edit_versions.Id: a newer approved revision staff reviewed and chose not to apply

Item responses add Upstream_Change (the approved revision's ID, headline and body) when the submission's approved revision differs from Source_Version_Id and has not been reviewed; the Builder offers Use approved copy or Keep edition copy.

docs.title: Operational extension tables
docs.text:
• harvested_events: Trumba occurrences keyed by source type/id, with independent SLC and ops triage status, source content hashes, change acknowledgment markers and promoted submission provenance.
  • ops_need_assessments: one need per harvested event, with confidence, rationale, AI/staff source and staff verdict. Child rows cascade when their event is deleted. Model/prompt identifiers are not stored per assessment today; this remains a provenance gap for auditability.
  • product_feedback: contact email, free-text report and client-provided browser context plus staff triage/GitHub references and disabled notification delivery state. Reported UI role is not a verified actor identity.

See the data dictionary for all columns.

docs.title: Controlled vocabularies
docs.text: The generated reference inventory lists all current seed groups/codes and documents code-governed exceptions. Live deployments can contain runtime additions; seeds are a bootstrap baseline. Review runtime changes back into seed/catalog metadata rather than automatically overwriting production.

docs.title: Derived and JSON Fields
docs.text: Field Table Lifecycle Flags edit_versions Created by rule-based pre-analysis and LLM response parsing Changes_Made edit_versions Created from AI response and editor workflow Excluded_Dates submission_schedule_requests, recurring_messages Maintained by skip/reschedule and recurring-message workflows Occurrence_Dates API response only Derived by recurrence service; not stored as a column Run_Number newsletter_items Calculated when assembling an issue based on prior placements

docs.title: Governance maintenance
docs.text:
The versioned catalog in frontend/src/data/governance-catalog.json drives the staff page and generated dictionary. scripts/check_governance.py compares every mapped column and vocabulary reference and checks generated pages in CI. This is a file-backed catalog; it is not a database DataDictionary table.

Classifications and retention categories are provisional pending owner review. See Governance decisions and Retention and disposal for unresolved approval, archive/disposal, lifecycle transition, runtime vocabulary reconciliation and production evidence requirements. No automatic purge is implemented.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Tool Version Notes Python 3.12+ Required for backend Node.js 22+ Required for frontend PostgreSQL 15+ Production only (SQLite for dev) Docker 24+ Required for production deploys

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
cd backend

# Create and activate virtual environment
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate   # macOS/Linux
# .venv\Scripts\activate    # Windows

# Install dependencies
pip install -e ".[dev]"

# Configure environment
cp ../.env.example .env
# Edit .env with your settings (see below)

# Apply migrations and seed reference data
alembic upgrade head
python -m app.db.seed

# Start the dev server
uvicorn app.main:app --port 8001 --reload --no-access-log --log-config logging.json

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
cd frontend

# Install dependencies
npm install

# Start the dev server
npm run dev

The Vite dev server starts on port 5173 and proxies /api requests to the backend at port 8001.

Optional frontend-only Vite settings, such as VITE_APP_ENV, can be placed in frontend/.env.local for local npm run dev sessions. Docker deployments read the same values from the project-level environment file and pass them into the frontend build.

Every page displays a persistent environment banner, including the sign-in page. Browser tabs use [DEV], [PROD], or [LOCAL] titles. Development and production store separate work; the development banner links to production. The two deployed hostnames determine both the visible label and feedback environment metadata, even when a production frontend build is used on dev. For custom preview hosts, set VITE_APP_ENV explicitly. Use VITE_APP_ENV=development in the dev deployment environment file and VITE_APP_ENV=production in production.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Create a .env file in the project root (for Docker) or backend/ directory (for local dev):

# Database (SQLite for development)
DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:///./ucm_newsletter.db

# App environment
ENVIRONMENT=development

# LLM Provider ("claude", "openai", or "mindrouter")
LLM_PROVIDER=claude

# Anthropic (required when LLM_PROVIDER=claude)
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
CLAUDE_MODEL=claude-sonnet-4-20250514

# OpenAI (required when LLM_PROVIDER=openai)
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4o
