docs.title: Feedback notifications
docs.text:
Feedback capture is database-first: a report is committed before any delivery attempt, and notification failure never discards the report. Staff can see new report counts and delivery state in the application.

Phase one does not send feedback outside the application. Keep the notification channel explicitly disabled in every environment:

FEEDBACK_NOTIFICATION_CHANNEL=disabled

The notification payload boundary is intentionally privacy-limited to feedback ID, type, summary, route, environment, submission time, and an optional contact email. It excludes report details, browser and host strings, submission content, submitter records, and editorial notes. Add and document an outbound adapter only after UCM and OIT approve the destination and credential model.

Port Conflict

Port 8000 may be in use by another application. This project defaults to port 8001 for the backend.

docs.title: Database Seeding
docs.text:
The seed script populates the database with controlled vocabularies and reference data: AllowedValue records, newsletter sections, style rules, schedule configs, and blackout dates. These tables are load-bearing — empty tables break dropdowns, validations, and FK lookups across the app.

The seed script assumes the schema already exists. Run Alembic migrations before seeding; production schema changes must come only from checked-in migrations, not SQLAlchemy metadata creation at app startup.

docs.title: Docker deployments
docs.text:
Seeding runs automatically on every backend container start via backend/docker-entrypoint.sh. No manual step required. The entrypoint runs in order: alembic upgrade head → python -m app.db.seed → uvicorn.

Seeding is idempotent and preserves existing staff-edited records by default. SEED_OVERWRITE=1 deliberately resets governed seed-backed configuration; review and back up changes before using it.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
For a local (non-Docker) dev server, run the seed script once after creating your venv and applying migrations:

cd backend
source .venv/bin/activate
alembic upgrade head
python -m app.db.seed

docs.title: Running one-off commands in the container
docs.text:
The entrypoint only runs the migrate-and-seed preamble when the container is starting the server (CMD begins with uvicorn). Other commands skip it:

docker compose exec backend alembic revision --autogenerate -m "..."
docker compose exec backend python -m app.db.seed    # re-seed manually
docker compose exec backend bash

docs.title: Running Dev Servers
docs.text:
Start both servers in separate terminals:

Terminal 1 -- Backend: 

cd backend && source .venv/bin/activate
uvicorn app.main:app --port 8001 --reload --no-access-log --log-config logging.json

Terminal 2 -- Frontend: 

cd frontend
npm run dev

Access the application at http://localhost:5173. The API is also directly available at http://localhost:8001/api/v1/.

Interactive API docs are served at http://localhost:8001/docs (Swagger UI) and http://localhost:8001/redoc (ReDoc).

docs.title: Docker Production Deployment
docs.text:
The project uses Docker Compose with two application containers connected to an external PostgreSQL network:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Docker Network (custom 10.x.x.x subnet)                │
│                                                          │
│  ┌────────────┐   ┌────────────┐                        │
│  │  frontend   │──>│  backend   │──> external Postgres  │
│  │  (nginx)    │   │ (uvicorn)  │    on insight-db-net  │
│  │  :80        │   │  :8001     │                        │
│  └──────┬─────┘   └────────────┘                        │
│         │                                                │
└─────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
          │
     HOST_PORT (9280/9290)
  • frontend (nginx) -- the only container with a host port mapping. Serves the React build and reverse-proxies /api/ to the backend.
  • backend (uvicorn) -- internal only, port 8001 on the Docker network.
  • database -- external PostgreSQL instance reachable on the insight-db-net Docker network.

docker-compose.yml does not create a database container. You must supply DATABASE_URL in the environment and ensure the shared insight-db-net external network already exists on the target host.

The deploy script rebuilds the stack, which triggers the backend entrypoint to run alembic upgrade head and seed reference data, and then smoke-tests the frontend and key API routes before returning success.

AI task recovery requires migration e9a1b3c5d7f2. Keep the backend at one process/replica: startup marks unfinished tasks interrupted for staff retry. Set AI_EDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY (default 2) and AI_EDIT_MAX_PENDING (default 50) to bound model work and queued requests. Completed task results and saved edits are committed together and survive restarts. See AI editing.

All .env and .env.* files, including .env.prod, are ignored by Git except the non-secret .env.example template. Never force-add environment files. Both Docker build contexts exclude environment files, and CI rejects tracked variants other than .env.example. Restrict server files to their owner with chmod 600 .env.prod (or .env for dev).

# Database
DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://ucm:<password>@insight-db:5432/ucm_newsletter
# For dev, point to the dev database instead:

docs.title: Prototype Staff Access
docs.text:
For advanced prototype testing, the frontend nginx container can assert a single trusted role for every proxied API request. Set both values in the environment file:

TRUSTED_ROLE_HEADER_SECRET=<random-long-secret>
TRUSTED_ROLE_HEADER_ROLE=staff

docker-compose.yml passes the secret to both containers. The frontend proxy overwrites X-Trusted-User-Role and X-Trusted-Auth-Secret before forwarding requests to the backend, and FastAPI accepts staff-only routes only when the secret matches.

The recognized trusted roles are staff (all editor tools; also passes every role-gated page), slc (the SLC calendar, triage, and digest pages), and ops (the /ops-triage page for Event Services). Asserting staff is the usual prototype choice since it satisfies every gate. For local (non-Docker) development, set DEV_TRUSTED_ROLE / DEV_TRUSTED_SECRET in frontend/.env.local and the matching TRUSTED_ROLE_HEADER_SECRET in backend/.env; the Vite proxy injects the headers.

This mode is the prototype boundary: everyone who can reach the URL gets the asserted role. Production should run on Single Sign-On instead.

docs.title: Single Sign-On (Microsoft Entra ID)
docs.text:
With AUTH_PROVIDER=oidc, users sign in with their University account. The backend runs the OIDC authorization-code flow as a Web (confidential) client, reads the user's Entra App Roles, and mints this application's own session token, which the browser presents as a bearer token on every request. Anonymous submitters are unaffected: /submit and the public API stay open.

The design mirrors the campus-services-maintenance application (its ADR-004), which OIT has already reviewed. See docs/adr/001-entra-sso.md.

What to request from OIT (one registration, or one per environment):

Item Value Registration type Web (confidential) client Reply URLs https://ucmnews-dev.insight.uidaho.edu/api/v1/auth/callback and https://ucmnews.insight.uidaho.edu/api/v1/auth/callback Front-channel logout / post-logout URL https://ucmnews.insight.uidaho.edu/ (and the dev host) App Roles three roles whose names you then put in ENTRA_GROUP_STAFF / _SLC / _OPS Scopes openid email profile (the default; no admin consent)

If OIT provisions Entra security groups instead of App Roles, set OIDC_GROUP_SOURCE=graph and put the group display names in the same ENTRA_GROUP_* variables. That path calls Microsoft Graph during sign-in and needs the delegated GroupMember.Read.All scope, which is an admin-consent request.

Enabling it on a deployed environment:

  1. Generate two distinct secrets: python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))" for SECRET_KEY and again for SESSION_COOKIE_SECRET.
  2. Fill the ENTRA_* / OIDC_* values in the environment file. The redirect URLs must be the public https:// hostname; the backend refuses to boot in production otherwise.
  3. Set AUTH_PROVIDER=oidc and blank TRUSTED_ROLE_HEADER_ROLE.
  4. ./deploy.sh <dev|prod>. The script adds two smoke checks under oidc: /api/v1/auth/config reports sso_enabled: true, and /api/v1/auth/sso/login redirects to login.microsoftonline.com.
  5. Sign in as one person per role and confirm each lands on the right view.

Rollback is AUTH_PROVIDER=header and a redeploy; there is no database migration to reverse.

Operational notes:

  • The client secret OIT issues expires 24 months after issue. Sign-in stops the day it lapses. Record the rotation date here when the secret is delivered: not yet issued.
  • A role revoked in Entra takes effect at the user's next sign-in; an outstanding session token stays valid until it expires (ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES, default 8 hours).
  • Signing out goes through Entra's end_session_endpoint so the next person at a shared computer is not silently signed in as the last one.
  • Under oidc, the nginx container still forwards X-Trusted-* headers with whatever TRUSTED_ROLE_HEADER_ROLE is set to. Leave it blank for clarity; the backend ignores those headers under oidc, so they grant nothing.

docs.title: Nginx Proxy Timeouts
docs.text:
The frontend nginx config includes extended timeouts for the /api/ proxy to accommodate slower on-prem model inference:

Directive Value Purpose proxy_read_timeout 300s MindRouter AI edits can take several minutes proxy_connect_timeout 10s Fast fail on backend unreachable proxy_send_timeout 60s Allow large request bodies

docker ps --filter "name=ucmnews"

# Check backend logs
docker logs ucmnews-prod-backend-1 --tail 50

# Run the full deploy workflow
./deploy.sh prod

docs.title: Scheduled SLC Harvest
docs.text: The SLC triage workflow depends on regular harvests of the U of I Trumba events feed: a harvest pulls new events into /slc-triage, and it is the only moment upstream edits, cancellations, and disappearances of flagged events are detected and badged. The repository deliberately has no in-process scheduler (no APScheduler or Celery); scheduling belongs to the deployment layer.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
backend/scripts/harvest_slc_events.py is the scheduled counterpart of the triage page's "Refresh events" button and POST /api/v1/slc/harvest — all three call the same harvest service. It is a dry run unless --apply is given. Invoke it as a module (-m) so the app package resolves in the container, which has no editable install of the backend package:

# Local development (from backend/, venv active)
python -m scripts.harvest_slc_events            # dry run: report what would change
python -m scripts.harvest_slc_events --apply    # persist the harvest

# Inside a deployed backend container
docker exec ucmnews-dev-backend-1 python -m scripts.harvest_slc_events --apply

Each run prints one timestamped line of counts:

[APPLY] 2026-08-28T06:15:02 fetched=200 created=3 updated=1 unchanged=196 canceled=0 skipped=0

canceled counts existing events newly canceled by that harvest (feed-marked or disappeared from the feed) — a nonzero value is the signal that flagged events may need attention on /slc-triage. Failures (network error, feed shape change) print a clear error to stderr and exit nonzero without touching existing rows, so cron can detect and report them.

An apply run then classifies operational needs for /ops-triage (events new or changed since their last assessment) and prints a second counts line:

[CLASSIFY] 2026-08-28T06:15:09 assessed=3 failed=0 pending=0

Classifier trouble — MindRouter down, malformed output — never fails the harvest: the run logs the problem, pending stays nonzero, and the next successful run catches up.

docker exec with a non-uvicorn command skips the entrypoint's migrate-and-seed preamble, so the scheduled run starts immediately against the already-migrated database.

docs.title: Cron on the deployment host
docs.text:
Schedule the harvest with the host crontab on the target server, one line per environment, writing to a log file so outcomes and drift stay visible:

# crontab -e as the devops user on openera.insight.uidaho.edu
15 * * * * docker exec ucmnews-dev-backend-1  python -m scripts.harvest_slc_events --apply >> /home/devops/UCMDailyRegister/logs/harvest-dev.log  2>&1
45 * * * * docker exec ucmnews-prod-backend-1 python -m scripts.harvest_slc_events --apply >> /home/devops/UCMDailyRegister/logs/harvest-prod.log 2>&1

Create the log directory once (mkdir -p /home/devops/UCMDailyRegister/logs). Hourly is comfortably fresh for the weekly SLC cadence and trivial in cost (one 200-row feed fetch); the two environments are offset so they never fetch at the same moment. Check recent outcomes with:

tail -n 24 /home/devops/UCMDailyRegister/logs/harvest-dev.log

A [ERROR] line means that run changed nothing; the next successful run catches up, since harvesting is idempotent. If runs must alert someone, set MAILTO in the crontab or wrap the line in the site's monitoring runner.

An alternative for hosts where the crontab is unavailable is a lightweight cron sidecar container in docker-compose.yml that runs the same docker exec-equivalent command on a schedule; the host crontab is preferred here because the deploy host already runs both environments' containers.

docs.title: Production Considerations
docs.text:
Production Checklist
  • Database -- set DATABASE_URL explicitly to the assigned shared Postgres database
  • CORS -- restrict CORS_ORIGINS to the production frontend domain
  • File uploads -- configure persistent storage for submission images (Docker volume or mounted directory)
  • HTTPS -- terminate TLS at a reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy, or cloud load balancer)
  • Secrets -- load API keys from environment variables, not committed .env files
  • Migrations -- migrations and seeding run automatically in the backend container entrypoint on every start
  • Backups -- the pgdata Docker volume should be backed up regularly

docs.title: Release evidence
docs.text:
Before production promotion, run python scripts/check_governance.py and the strict documentation build. Record commit/image digests, per-role sign-in checks, AI endpoint/model approvals, backup/expiry installation and a paired restore exercise in Governance decisions. Local tests are not proof of deployed configuration. Follow Backup and recovery for migration-compatible rollback; do not start old code before checking schema compatibility. Docker stdout uses bounded rotation and minimized JSON; campus ingress logging and time-based retention still need verification.

Generate SBOMs and vulnerability reports from the actual release environment, not an unrelated developer virtualenv. Historical files under sbom/ remain dated reference artifacts until a release-bound replacement is collected.

docs.title: Documentation and data governance audit
docs.text:
Assessment date: October 22, 2026. Assessed repository revision: b7d893b1209ead93ad08dd2daae36fe7c953cff6. Assessor: Codex.

Follow-up: Remediation status. Findings below describe the assessed revision, not the remediated working tree.

Correction: DG-05 originally described /settings/ai as staff-gated. It is public metadata in the assessed code. Its lack of DB/readiness verification, rather than an OIDC permission failure, is the reason to replace it as a health probe. This correction does not change the recovery finding's other evidence.

docs.title: Assessment
docs.text:
The project has a useful documentation baseline, but its governance artifacts are not reliable as a current inventory or as evidence that documented controls operate. This review identifies 13 findings: five high and eight medium. The highest priorities are privacy inventory accuracy, authentication guidance, retention/disposal, sensitive logging, and recovery procedures.

Strengths include domain explanations in model modules, Alembic migrations, database-backed vocabularies, a staff-facing governance catalog, an explicit Entra decision record, documented gaps, and a machine-readable evidence manifest that separates compliance assertions from issue state. CI checks PostgreSQL migration drift. These provide a practical foundation for remediation.

docs.title: Scope and limits
docs.text:
Reviewed README and agent conventions, MkDocs configuration and pages, security and SBOM artifacts, governance JSON and its schema, ORM declarations, bootstrap data, authentication and authorization, relevant data flows, Compose, and CI. Code inspection corroborates documentation findings; this is not a full security or application-code audit.

This is a repository assessment. Production configuration, database contents, backup schedules and restore records, institutional approvals, live GitHub issue states, and the neighboring portfolio governance repository were not verified. An absent repository reference means evidence is missing here, not that an institutional activity never occurred. External policies, vendor contracts, and legal conclusions were not reassessed. Historical audits retain their original dates and should not be treated as current verification.

High means incorrect or incomplete guidance could materially affect privacy, access decisions, disposal, or recovery. Medium means inventory, traceability, or maintenance assurance needs correction.

docs.title: Verified inventory and checks
docs.text:
Check Result ORM declarations 19 tables, 197 mapped columns, counted from Python AST Staff governance catalog 16 tables, 143 columns; all listed columns exist in ORM declarations Catalog omissions Three tables containing 49 columns, plus five columns in existing tables AllowedValue bootstrap 16 groups, 60 values; data-model docs say 10 groups, 41 values Other bootstrap data 15 sections, 99 style rules, six schedule configurations Evidence manifest All 15 requirements validate against Draft 2020-12 schema, including format checking; all repository source paths exist Assertion freshness All 15 assertions have validated_at: 2026-05-05 Assertion states Eight partially_aligned, four gap, three needs_decision Schema negative probes Missing repo_file.path and duplicate requirement IDs are both accepted Strict documentation build Passed; five pre-existing Markdown pages are outside navigation Focused backend verification 80 tests passed across authorization, SSO, images, and feedback; one Authlib deprecation warning

AST counts describe checked-in models, not a live database. Seed counts describe bootstrap data, not expected production row counts. Passing documentation and schema builds does not establish factual accuracy.

docs.title: DG-01 — High: Privacy inventory omits current identity and feedback data
docs.text:
Evidence: docs/data-governance.md:17 inventories only five submission fields and line 29 says authentication tokens are not collected. backend/app/models/feedback.py:35 stores contact email and free-text report details alongside browser, host, and route context. backend/app/api/v1/sso.py:207 uses email/username as the session subject; backend/app/auth/session_tokens.py:23 mints a token carrying subject, name, and role. frontend/src/auth/tokenStore.ts:56 reads that token from localStorage. The ADR's statement that nothing about a person is persisted (docs/adr/001-entra-sso.md:62) overlooks browser storage.

Impact: Reviewers and users receive an incomplete account of identifiable data and storage locations. No user table does not mean no identity persistence.

Remediation: Inventory feedback, identity claims, browser token storage, OIDC state cookies, authentication logs, free text, and exports. State purpose, classification, access, retention, and deletion behavior for each. Replace absolute non-collection claims with the application's intended scope and actual handling. Add the submitter-facing privacy notice already listed as open work. Suggested accountable roles: data steward and authentication maintainer.

docs.title: DG-02 — High: Governance access matrix contradicts implemented authorization
docs.text:
Evidence: docs/data-governance.md:81 and line 235 describe header-only roles and no individual identity. Its matrix at line 229 omits ops and says SLC cannot edit records. backend/app/api/deps.py supports mutually exclusive header/OIDC modes and staff/SLC/ops guards; backend/app/api/v1/slc_events.py and backend/app/api/v1/ops_events.py expose triage mutations. Public feedback creation is also absent from the matrix. The API reference and deployment guide already explain both authentication modes.

Impact: Staff cannot use the governance matrix to determine who can view or change which datasets. Header mode can grant the proxy's configured role to every reachable visitor, a limitation documented more clearly elsewhere.

Remediation: Publish a route/dataset permission matrix for public, staff, SLC, and ops, including triage, needs verdicts, feedback, exports, and PII redaction. Describe header and OIDC behavior separately. Record verified mode per environment and evidence of role-by-role validation before asserting production protection. Suggested owner: authentication maintainer.

docs.title: DG-03 — High: Retention policy lacks an executable, internally consistent disposal design
docs.text:
Evidence: docs/data-governance.md:163 specifies two academic years for submissions, indefinite newsletters, and 90 days for imported content. Line 175 would purge newsletter item references with a submission. No scheduled retention implementation was found. backend/app/services/submission_service.py:240 deletes an ORM record without deleting its uploaded file. backend/app/models/newsletter.py:87 retains a required submission FK; Source_Version_Id and Upstream_Reviewed_Version_Id add version dependencies.

Impact: The retention table is not evidence of enforcement. Deleting publication placements could undermine the indefinite issue archive; deleting only submission rows does not dispose of associated files. Feedback, harvested events, ops assessments, identity data, and backup copies lack complete rules.

Remediation: Define the retention clock, academic-year boundary, exceptions and holds, owners, and disposal evidence. Decide how to preserve published issue snapshots while removing contact data and source history. Specify FK ordering, file removal, backup expiry, restored-data handling, and all newer datasets before implementing a dry-run-capable cleanup job. Suggested owners: data steward and backend maintainer.

docs.title: DG-04 — High: Actual logging conflicts with the documented PII prohibition
docs.text:
Evidence: Audit logging says PII must never appear in logs. backend/app/api/v1/sso.py:230, line 235, and line 238 log the subject, which is an email/username. backend/app/utils/hyperlinks.py:76 and related branches log complete wrapped and destination URLs; their query strings can contain identifiers or tokens. AI error paths also interpolate exception text (backend/app/services/ai/editor.py:507).

Impact: If those log levels are enabled, identity and potentially sensitive URL data enter a channel absent from the privacy inventory. The documented 90-day/one-year retention targets have no linked operational evidence.

Remediation: Define a deliberate identity-logging policy, use minimized identifiers where appropriate, remove or redact URL query/fragment values, and sanitize external error details. Classify remaining logs and record destination, access, expiry, reviewer, and verification evidence. Test representative sensitive values. Suggested owners: security reviewer and backend maintainer.

docs.title: DG-05 — High: Recovery runbook can produce misleading checks and lacks recoverable upload versions
docs.text:
Evidence: docs/backup-and-recovery.md:55 syncs all upload backups into one directory without dated snapshots or deletion, while claiming database-equivalent retention. Lines 135 and 249 use /settings/ai metadata as a health probe. Line 250 imports the database engine without executing a database query. Lines 166–177 rebuild the old application before describing migration downgrade. No completed restore record is linked. The daily cron entries are examples, not proof of installed jobs.

Impact: The upload example cannot provide the stated historical retention; removed files can accumulate. The settings check does not verify database readiness, and an engine import can pass without a working database. Rollback ordering and an unspecified one-step downgrade are unsafe assumptions for arbitrary releases.

Remediation: Use versioned upload backups paired with database recovery points and bounded expiry. Use /health for liveness and /readyz for database and reference-data readiness. Describe release-specific migration compatibility, pre-rollback backup and preservation steps, and validation before restoring traffic. Link a dated restore exercise and measured RPO/RTO. Suggested owner: operations maintainer.

docs.title: DG-06 — Medium: AI data-flow and processor assurances are incomplete
docs.text:
Evidence: docs/data-governance.md:88 describes newsletter editing and notes-based PII risk, but does not enumerate provided links and their parameters or the ops classifier. backend/app/services/ai/prompts.py transmits links and editor instructions and can send original input, draft text, and findings in a repair request. backend/app/services/ai/ops_needs_classifier.py separately processes harvested title, description, location, and category through a configurable MindRouter endpoint. The provider table at line 108 makes residency and handling assertions without linked contract or configuration evidence.

Impact: Reviewers lack the complete input/output lineage and evidence needed to approve each AI use. Excluding dedicated contact columns does not exclude contacts embedded in content, links, instructions, or generated rationales.

Remediation: Document both AI workflows, repair requests, outputs, stored provenance, and endpoint configuration. Link approved processor/model decisions, retention and residency evidence, and external-provider exceptions. Distinguish training restrictions from retention and location. No vendor compliance claim is made by this audit. Suggested owner: AI service maintainer and data steward.

docs.title: DG-07 — Medium: Schema, catalog, and vocabulary documentation have measurable drift
docs.text:
Evidence: Data model and UDM alignment still describe 16 tables. frontend/src/pages/DataGovernancePage.tsx:46 contains 16 of the 19 current tables. Missing tables are product_feedback, harvested_events, and ops_need_assessments (49 columns). Missing columns in existing catalog entries are submissions.Approved_Version_Id and newsletter_items.Manually_Placed, Source_Version_Id, Edition_Edited, and Upstream_Reviewed_Version_Id. Data-model vocabulary counts are 10/41 against 16/60 in the seed file. Six new groups cover SLC/ops review and ops needs.

Impact: The staff catalog omits entire operational datasets and editorial provenance. Manual copies have already diverged. Vocabulary conventions are also overstated: SLC event classification is still a schema regex, and the edit-history docstring claims an AI provider vocabulary not present in the bootstrap groups.

Remediation: Establish one versioned machine-readable catalog with complete column definitions, PII risk, retention, steward, sources, and vocabulary mapping; generate or validate the UI and prose against it. Update the ERD and vocabulary inventory and explicitly document intentionally code-governed exceptions. Check the neighboring portfolio registry separately before repeating its asserted current state. Suggested owner: data steward and schema maintainer.

docs.title: DG-08 — Medium: Evidence manifest is structurally valid but semantically stale
docs.text:
Evidence: All 15 assertions in docs/governance/enterprise-ai-framework/evidence.json are dated May 5, 2026. The auth summary at line 104 says no Entra implementation or group mapping exists; both are now in code. The approved-stack matrix similarly says there is no OIDC session implementation. All linked repository paths exist, which does not establish that the assertions accurately describe their contents.

Impact: Aggregators can ingest obsolete conclusions successfully. Mutable file paths do not identify the revision actually reviewed.

Remediation: Revalidate each assertion against a commit, add artifact/review dates and responsible reviewers, and reconcile the matrix with the manifest. Separate implemented code, environment enablement, test evidence, and formal approval. Entra code alone is insufficient to mark production alignment. Suggested owner: governance evidence maintainer.

docs.title: DG-09 — Medium: CI does not enforce documentation or governance freshness
docs.text:
Evidence: .github/workflows/docs.yml publishes on main with mkdocs gh-deploy --force; it does not run a strict PR build. .github/workflows/ci.yml checks application code and Alembic drift, but not catalog completeness, seed/documentation consistency, or the evidence schema. The evidence schema accepts both a repo_file with no path and duplicate requirement IDs in negative probes.

Impact: The existing green checks permit both factual drift and ambiguous evidence primary keys. Alembic drift checks address a different contract.

Remediation: Add PR checks for strict docs, evidence validation with formats, type-specific evidence source fields and existence, unique requirement IDs, catalog/ORM coverage, and governed seed mappings. Define a review freshness policy. Preserve the distinction between issue state and compliance assertion. Suggested owner: CI maintainer.

docs.title: DG-10 — Medium: Classification and privacy conclusions lack reviewable approval evidence
docs.text:
Evidence: docs/data-governance.md:11 classifies unpublished original copy as Public by intended use; the UI applies the same label to original and version content. Line 159 makes an unconditional FERPA conclusion. The repository's own classification evidence item records a missing APM 30.11 mapping; no signed data owner classification decision is linked.

Impact: Intended publication can be confused with approved disclosure, and free-text content can exceed the assumed scope. The documents do not establish the authority or evidence behind the categorical privacy conclusion.

Remediation: Request steward/security review of working-copy and publication classifications, incidental sensitive data, mixed datasets, and institutional classification mapping. Record decision owner, date, scope, and approval reference. Present FERPA scope as an assessed assumption pending the appropriate institutional review; this audit makes no legal determination. Suggested owner: data owner with privacy/security reviewer.

docs.title: DG-11 — Medium: Setup instructions and architecture facts contradict the current repository
docs.text:
Evidence: README.md:33 puts .env in the root while its commands execute from backend/; Settings reads .env relative to the working directory. docs/deployment.md:28 copies .env.example from inside backend/, where no template exists. docs/architecture.md:103 calls Compose a three-service stack, but it defines frontend/backend and an external database network. README seed counts say 14 sections, 37 rules, four schedule configs, and 10 value groups; current counts are 15, 99, six, and 16. Agent deployment conventions also describe a local database container and POSTGRES_PASSWORD that current Compose does not use. Agent AI descriptions do not match the actual provider set.

Impact: A new maintainer can follow setup successfully while loading no configured secrets, or fail at the copy step; deployment expectations diverge.

Remediation: Use cp ../.env.example .env for the shown local backend workflow, reconcile topology and provider guidance, and derive volatile counts from seed data. Review README, AGENTS, CLAUDE, architecture, and deployment as one set. Suggested owner: documentation maintainer.

docs.title: DG-12 — Medium: Ownership and non-production data decisions remain unassigned
docs.text:
Evidence: The ownership, dev/test data, local AI tooling, and intake items in the evidence manifest remain open assertions without linked final decisions. The governance UI has team-level steward labels, but lacks retention metadata and accountable review dates. The recovery guide instructs restoring production backups to a test database without an accompanying data protection procedure.

Impact: Known gaps can persist without a person responsible for closure; operators lack explicit rules for production data in tests, local AI tools, feedback exports, and restoration exercises.

Remediation: Record named accountable business, technical, and data owners with review cadence and escalation. Approve production-copy/scrubbing rules, protected restore testing, local AI handling, and feedback export review. Link institutional approvals or exceptions using non-sensitive references. Suggested owner: project sponsor with operations and data steward.

docs.title: DG-13 — Medium: SBOM and vulnerability artifacts cannot represent the current release
docs.text:
Evidence: sbom/README.md and both CycloneDX metadata timestamps are dated March 31, 2026. The backend SBOM lacks authlib, itsdangerous, and pyjwt, all now declared in backend/pyproject.toml. Regeneration is recommended, but CI has no SBOM freshness gate or release binding.

Impact: The artifacts omit current authentication dependencies and their historical vulnerability summaries cannot substantiate current release posture.

Remediation: Generate SBOMs from the actual release dependency environment and frontend lockfile; bind them to commit and image digest. Attach dated scan outputs and finding dispositions. This audit did not run a fresh vulnerability scan or assess current CVEs. Suggested owner: release maintainer.

docs.title: Remediation sequence and acceptance evidence
docs.text:
Sequence Work Completion evidence 1 Correct privacy and role guidance; reconcile logging policy Reviewed inventory and permission matrix; sensitive-value logging tests; identified environment auth evidence 2 Decide classification and disposal; repair recovery guidance Owner-approved decisions, complete retention matrix, dependency-aware disposal design, dated restore exercise 3 Refresh catalog, vocabulary, AI lineage, and evidence assertions Complete 19-table/197-column catalog, 16-group/60-value bootstrap mapping, reviewed AI flow and processor references, commit-bound evidence 4 Close ownership/process gaps and add drift gates Named owners, approved handling procedures, PR checks, release-bound SBOMs, reproducible setup instructions

Suggested roles above are proposed assignments, not accepted commitments. No policy approvals, live deployments, issue updates, or runtime changes were made as part of this audit.

docs.title: Reproduction
docs.text:
Run from the repository root with the relevant dependencies installed:

python3 -m mkdocs build --strict --site-dir /tmp/ucm-documentation-audit-site
backend/.venv/bin/python -m pytest backend/tests/test_authorization.py backend/tests/test_auth_sso.py backend/tests/test_images.py backend/tests/test_feedback.py -q
git diff --check

The inventory comparison parsed each model class's __tablename__ and mapped_column declarations with Python AST and compared their names with GOVERNANCE_TABLES/col() entries in the frontend source. Seed totals came directly from JSON arrays. Manifest validation used Draft202012Validator(schema, format_checker=FormatChecker()), followed by existence checks for every repo_file and repo_directory source. Schema negative probes operated on in-memory copies only.

docs.title: Joy's Feedback Digest — prepared 2026-07-17
docs.text:
Source: product_feedback table, production database (ucm_newsletter on insight-db). 48 reports total (43 from jbauer@uidaho.edu, 5 anonymous filed in the same sessions), 2026-05-14 → 2026-07-17. All 48 still have status new.

Report numbers below refer to chronological order (1 = oldest).

docs.title: Theme 1 — The off-by-one date bug (her most-reported issue; root cause identified)
docs.text:
Reports 9, 26, 44, 47 all describe the same thing: she requests a run date (e.g. Monday 6/29 or 7/20), and staff view / the Builder header shows the day before (Sunday 6/28, 7/19). Report 47 opens with "I've brought this one to your attention before."

Reports 5, 25, 40, 41–42, 43 are very likely the same bug wearing different costumes: - 5 & 43: Builder shows the wrong day's entries / no entries for a date she knows has items. - 25: "Sunday should not be a selectable option" — a Monday shifted back a day renders as Sunday. - 40: Monday Oct. 5 rejected as invalid for My UI — consistent with it being validated as Sunday Oct. 4. - 41–42: dates rejected as "not a valid publication date."

Root cause (from today's code audit): date-only strings parsed as UTC midnight (new Date('2026-07-20')) render/validate one day earlier in Mountain time. Confirmed in BuilderPage.tsx:1085, BuilderPage.tsx:1317, SubmissionMeta.tsx:187/203/229; UTC "today" math in SchedulePrefs.tsx, SubmissionMeta.tsx, BuilderPage.tsx. Other pages already use the safe +'T12:00:00' pattern. Fixing this one bug likely resolves ~9 of her 48 reports.

docs.title: Theme 2 — Manual edit destroys the original submission (root cause identified)
docs.text:
Reports 12, 29: saving a manual/final edit overwrites the Original view; "We always need a record of what was originally submitted that remains intact." Related asks: 11 (show original beside the manual-edit window), 12 (let her edit the AI version directly, side-by-side with original).

Root cause (from audit): POST /ai-edits/{id}/finalize overwrites Original_Headline/Original_Body (backend/app/api/v1/ai_edits.py:313). If no AI edit ran first, the submitter's original is unrecoverable.

docs.title: Theme 3 — AI style-rule adjustments (13 reports; these are her editing the prompt via the bug tracker)
docs.text:
Reports 2, 3, 10, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 27, 28, 30 each contain a ready-to-use style rule: - Times: noon/midnight, "to" vs hyphen across a.m./p.m., full AP time rules (28) - Headlines: sentence case but capitalize proper nouns (10, 30 — see Theme 4) - Acronyms: spell out on first reference (13) - Spell out state names (14); "&" → "and" (15) - Don't touch event titles' title case (16) - Event info order: time, day, date, location (17, also 39) - "MDT" → "Mountain time" (18); periods on directional abbreviations (19) - Short sentences, no semicolons (27) - Overall tone/structure prompt rewrite (3)

These are mostly data changes in the Style Rules UI, not code. ⚠️ But note audit finding: the seed script force-reverts style-rule text on every redeploy (backend/app/db/seed.py:106, run by docker-entrypoint.sh). If rules were added in the UI and later reverted, that explains Theme 4.

docs.title: Theme 4 — "I reported this and it's still broken" (trust erosion)
docs.text: Reports 21, 30, 38: headline proper-noun capitalization reported three times over three weeks; "It does not respond to Editor feedback... It makes no changes after I select Revise." Report 34 (jobs): "I believe I reported this last week... If this requires a call to sort out, please let me know." Candidate causes: seed reverting rule edits (Theme 3 warning), and/or editor feedback not persisting (Theme 5).

docs.title: Theme 5 — Editor feedback should teach the system, not just fix one item
docs.text: Reports 31, 39: feedback given in the AI controls applies only to the current submission; she wants it to update the instruction set for all future edits. This is a real feature request (feedback → persisted style rule), not a bug.

docs.title: Theme 6 — Job postings need a completely different pipeline
docs.text: Reports 8, 20, 22, 23, 34 (repeated, escalating): jobs should not get AI news-style editing or headlines. Wanted format: one line per job — Job title (sentence case), Department (capitalized), location (omit if Moscow) — as a live link, in a dedicated "Job opportunities" section at the bottom of the Builder. Remove "how many times to run" from the job submission form (jobs always run once, for two weeks).

docs.title: Theme 7 — Builder gaps
docs.text:
• 33: show the full approved entry text, not just the first sentence.
  • 45: "Academic dates and deadlines" drop-zone doesn't accept anything (she wants to pull from uidaho.edu/registrar/dates-deadlines).
  • 46: wants manual editing inside the Builder.
  • 35: new section under Employee Announcements: "Reminders for your students" (staff-only, not in submitter view).

docs.title: Theme 8 — Scope confusion / remove features
docs.text:
• 1: Auxiliary Services calendar spreadsheet import is flooding submissions with unusable items — remove it entirely.
  • 6, 7: doesn't know what the SLC calendar is or why it's in the tool ("Did someone else request it?").
  • 24: "Repeat on a cadence" should be staff-only, not in submitter view.

docs.title: Theme 9 — Links & URLs
docs.text:
• 32: in edit mode, links render as raw code/plain text; wants CTA text as a live link with the URL editable separately, and the ability to add URLs/CTAs while editing.
  • 37: accept email addresses as links, with a name field beside them.

docs.title: Theme 10 — Scheduling rules & settings (data/config)
docs.text:
• 36: My UI runs every Monday including holidays; TDR skips holidays — holiday blocking must be per-newsletter.
  • 48 (filed today): My UI submission deadline should be noon Wednesday during the academic year — Settings change.

docs.title: One-off
docs.text: • 4: two users got different AI results for the same submission — expected LLM nondeterminism; worth explaining (or lowering temperature) rather than "fixing."

docs.title: Suggested meeting talking points
docs.text:
1. Acknowledge the backlog: 48 reports received, none triaged — own it, then show the themes above so she knows they were heard.
  2. Quick wins to promise: the off-by-one date fix (kills ~9 reports), original-preservation fix, loading her 13 style-rule prompts.
  3. Decisions to ask of her: job-posting format sign-off (Theme 6), SLC calendar's future (Theme 8), "Reminders for your students" section details.
  4. Set expectations on Theme 5 (feedback that persists) — real feature, worth scoping together.

docs.text:
All 48 reports were exported to 13 issues; each product_feedback row now has Status=exported and its GitHub_URL set.

Issue Covers reports #192 UTC off-by-one dates 5, 9, 25, 26, 40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 47 #193 Finalize overwrites original 11, 12, 29 #194 13 AP-style rule adjustments 2, 3, 10, 13–19, 27, 28, 30 #195 Seed reverts style-rule edits 21, 38 #196 Persistent editor feedback 31, 39 #197 Job postings pipeline 8, 20, 22, 23, 34 #198 Builder: full text + manual edit 33, 46 #199 Builder: academic-dates drop-zone 45 #200 Builder: "Reminders for your students" 35 #201 My UI Monday/holiday rules + deadline 36, 40*, 48 #202 CTA links + email links 32, 37 #203 Scope decisions (Aux import, SLC, cadence) 1, 6, 7, 24 #204 AI nondeterminism between users 4
